You are a code worker on the freytag-forge repository at /home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge. Boundary: NO model call, NO network call, never git commit, never git add. Every test you write must be hermetic (fake the Jev ask and the narrator reply; no live Worker). Edit ONLY these files: storygame/runtime/jev_questions.py, storygame/runtime/taking.py, storygame/runtime/capture.py, storygame/runtime/item_facts.py, bench/jev_use.py, bench/core.py, tests/test_taking.py, tests/test_jev_questions.py, tests/test_jev_use.py, tests/test_held_by_echo.py, tests/test_bench.py, tests/test_runtime_capture.py. Do not touch story data, docs, other tests or other source. Write the failing tests first, run them to see them fail, then make the change.

PROBLEM (diagnosed from a live run). In scene 1A the player typed 'Pick up the phone.' The narrator's item_facts reply was {"phone": {"held_by": "Kristin", "place": "Michelle's kitchen", "owner": "Michelle"}}. ItemFactsProvider.apply_item_facts in storygame/runtime/item_facts.py has a rule (added in commit fa3c837d, tested in tests/test_held_by_echo.py): when an entry has both 'held_by' X and a 'place' equal to the thing's CURRENT parent, and X is not that parent, the place is treated as an echo, held_by is dropped, and the thing stays put. That rule exists for a lamp that is only lit (the narrator wrongly adds held_by). Here it wrongly cancelled a real pickup, so the phone stayed 'on the kitchen floor', and the next turn's THINGS line told the narrator the phone was still on the floor. The engine cannot tell the two apart because its take step (take_before_put in storygame/runtime/taking.py) deliberately ignores pickup commands: the Jev question moves_thing in storygame/runtime/jev_questions.py answers false for 'The command already says to pick up or take the thing'.

FIX (design is decided; do not redesign). Let the engine know, per turn, which named loose things the command picks up, and let that knowledge break the tie in favour of held_by.
1. jev_questions.py: add a function (suggested name thing_command_kind(ask, command, thing_name)) that sends ONE Jev request carrying two noul questions, 'moves_thing' (existing wording, unchanged) and a new 'picks_up_thing' (true: the command says to pick up, take, grab, or lift the thing; false: it only looks at, reads, searches, talks about, puts, places, stores or hands over the thing, or does not mention taking it), and returns a pair (moves, picks_up), each bool or None. Keep moves_thing() and its payload unchanged. Reuse _answer/noul_yes style; an exception or missing key gives None for that member.
2. taking.py: TakingResult gains a field pickups: tuple[str, ...] = () holding entity ids the command picks up (keep the first four fields and positional construction working). take_before_put gains an optional keyword kind_of_thing: Callable[[str, str], tuple[bool | None, bool | None]] | None = None. When it is given, use it instead of the moves_thing callable for each candidate: moves True keeps today's behaviour (engine moves the thing to the protagonist and adds the step text); else picks_up True records the id in pickups and does NOT move the thing or add a step (the narrator narrates the pickup); moves None and picks_up None keeps today's 'taking question unanswered' issue. When kind_of_thing is None, behave exactly as today. A thing the protagonist already holds is not a candidate (takeable_items already filters this) so it can never be in pickups.
3. bench/jev_use.py: add ask_thing_command_kind mirroring ask_moves_thing. capture.py and bench/core.py (the call at about line 871) must pass kind_of_thing so the real runtime and the bench both use it; keep ask_moves_thing for existing tests.
4. item_facts.py: ItemFactsProvider gets a per-turn attribute (suggested pickup_ids, a frozenset of entity ids, default empty in __init__). capture.py sets it next to self.provider.prior_steps from taking.pickups on every turn, including the early-return and refusal paths (empty there), so it can never leak into the next turn. In the held_by conflict block of apply_item_facts, when entry_id is in pickup_ids and holder_id is the protagonist (self.state.package.world.protagonist_id), do NOT take the 'place echo wins' branch; make held_by win (value['place'] = the holder name, held_by popped) regardless of the echoed place. Every other case keeps today's behaviour exactly: an unflagged echo still keeps the thing in place, a flagged entry whose holder is someone else still follows today's rule, a held_by with a different place still moves to that place.

TESTS TO ADD (names are suggestions): (a) test_held_by_echo.py: the exact failure above on the synthetic package from tests/test_place_scoped_feed.py (_synthetic_package): lamp, place echoing the room, held_by the protagonist, lamp id in pickup_ids -> afterwards world.parent('lamp') is the protagonist and facts['lamp']['place'] is the protagonist's name; the same entry without pickup_ids still keeps the lamp in the room (existing test stays green); flagged but held_by another person (e.g. 'Mira') still drops the holder; flagged lamp with an owner key and a key name that needs resolving ('lamp' resolved from a bare word) also lands. (b) test_taking.py: with kind_of_thing returning (False, True) the thing is NOT moved, no step is added, result.pickups == (its id,), asked is True; (True, False) still moves and adds the step; (False, False) and (None, None) behave as today (nothing recorded; None gives the issue); with kind_of_thing=None the old moves_thing path is unchanged. (c) test_jev_questions.py and test_jev_use.py: one request body contains both question keys; answers parse to the pair; a failure gives (None, None). (d) test_runtime_capture.py or the closest existing capture test: after a turn whose command picks up a loose item the provider's pickup_ids contains it, and after the next non-pickup turn it is empty. (e) test_bench.py: the bench path passes kind_of_thing and records no taking step for a pickup. Update existing tests only where they assert the old call shape (for example a stub of ask_moves_thing that must now stub ask_thing_command_kind); never weaken an assertion that still holds.

Use the main virtualenv: cd to your working directory, then PYTHONPATH=$PWD:$PWD/packages/worldkeeper/src TMPDIR=/tmp /home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge/.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider <files>. First confirm python -c 'import storygame; print(storygame.__file__)' prints a path under your working directory. Run ruff as /home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge/.venv/bin/python -m ruff check <files> and -m ruff format <files> (repo is ruff-formatted; format the files you edit). Run the files you own, then the related suites: tests/test_taking.py tests/test_jev_questions.py tests/test_jev_use.py tests/test_held_by_echo.py tests/test_bench.py tests/test_runtime_capture.py tests/test_already_aboard_engine_reply.py tests/test_observation_resume.py tests/test_bench_item_facts.py tests/test_3c_item_facts_capture.py tests/test_3c_world_capture_wiring.py tests/test_item_facts_null_place.py tests/test_observation_held_relations.py tests/test_runtime_jev.py tests/test_jev_batching.py tests/test_place_scoped_feed.py. Output contract: the changed files above only, all of the named suites green, ruff clean. Report in your final message which tests you added and whether any existing test needed changing and why.
